title: I’m using AI-assisted asset workflows to build a dynamic water system for my solo voxel colony sim
author: Arrock12
selftext:
I’m solo-developing **StoneEra**, a voxel colony survival game where water is a system you can engineer around, rather than static scenery.

The video shows:

* Wind-powered pumps moving water through pipes
* Water wheels reacting to flowing water
* Channels built to redirect the flow
* Water responding dynamically when the terrain changes

The footage is recorded in creative mode so I can quickly demonstrate the complete setup. During normal gameplay, the player plans these structures, while villagers gather the required materials and construct them.

I’ve been using generative AI as an assistant during parts of the 3D asset workflow. It helps me explore initial ideas and iterate faster, but the generated result is never the finished game asset. I review it, edit the model and materials, adapt it to StoneEra’s voxel style, integrate it into Unity, and then build the gameplay systems around it myself.

For me, the difficult part isn’t generating an object. It’s making everything feel like it belongs in the same world and turning it into a functional game system with animation, construction rules, simulation, and performance constraints.

How are other solo developers using AI while keeping a consistent visual style across their game?

If the combination of colony building, editable terrain, and water engineering interests you, StoneEra is on Steam:

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5057770/StoneEra](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5057770/StoneEra/)
